neighboring_unit_entries.title: A convergence-equivalent prime-power series for zeta^(alpha)
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The section moves from the failure of a direct Euler-product derivative to Theorem 4.3, which replaces equality by joint convergence or divergence with a double prime-power series in Re(s)<0 and begins deriving it through the Grünwald–Letnikov limit and product-to-series comparison.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Because log^alpha destroys the direct multiplicative Euler-product route and derivative zeros are poorly controlled, the paper changes the target to convergence equivalence with a prime-power double series in a domain where geometric expansion and zeta^(alpha) convergence overlap.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The result is co-convergence rather than equality, applies only in the nonempty strip 1+alpha<Re(s)<0 with alpha<-1, and does not locate primes or zeros near Re(s)=1/2+alpha.
